market_mood: Cautious and rate-driven: stocks are holding up but wobbling as Fed hike bets, a 10-year yield above 5%, and an AI-leadership scare hit growth names.

themes.title: Hot CPI locks in a December Fed hike; 10-year yield above 5%
themes.what_happened: October CPI rose 0.4% against 0.3% expected, and core rose 0.3%. The 10-year yield rose above 5% on Thursday and was near 5.15% on Friday. CME FedWatch now prices a Dec. 9 hike at 100%, with about 14% odds of a 50bp move.
themes.why_it_matters: A faster tightening path raises the discount rate on long-duration growth stocks and pushes the dollar up, while gold fell roughly 3% on the week.

our_exposure.why: High-multiple AI leader; rising yields add to stock-specific pressure.
Large weight; capital-intensive utility with high sensitivity to rates and AI-power sentiment.
Firmer dollar and higher yields weighed on copper and the miners.
Higher rates support lending margins, but financials sector fell 0.7% Thursday.
Higher rates help net interest income; credit and equity-market risk offset.
Rate-sensitive AI hardware name in a Nasdaq that is selling off.
Long-duration software multiple compresses as yields climb.

themes.next: Fed speakers (Waller and Logan are already hawkish), 30-year Treasury demand, and the Dec. 9 FOMC meeting.

themes.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns; earnings Nov. 17 with no successor
themes.what_happened: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO effective immediately after a board probe into a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese government agent. NVDA fell about 4.3% Thursday after trading as much as 14% lower at the open. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 0.5% and a memory-supplier ETF fell 2.6%. Broadcom (+5.5%) and AMD (+5.9%) rose.
themes.why_it_matters: Nvidia is the S&P 500's heaviest weight and the AI trade's bellwether, so the leadership vacuum and a possible China-shipment fallout raise the stakes on its guidance.

our_exposure.why: Direct hit: leadership vacuum, scandal, and earnings risk next Tuesday.
Fell 1.6% Thursday; memory suppliers sold off with the AI complex.
Memory/storage name; memory ETF fell 2.6% Thursday.
Storage peer exposed to the same AI-capex sentiment swing.
AI data-center infrastructure; leans on Nvidia-driven buildout.
Competing AI silicon and models gain if Nvidia stumbles.

themes.next: Nvidia fiscal Q3 results Tuesday Nov. 17. LSEG consensus is about $109B revenue, and the guidance matters more than the quarter.

themes.title: Democratic midterm sweep and Anthropic IPO test the AI buildout
themes.what_happened: After the Democrats' gains in the midterms, the AI sector sold off on fears of tougher regulation and data-center scrutiny. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% last week. Anthropic set a $70–$78 IPO range, a roughly $1.4T valuation at the top end, to raise up to $64.4B. Pricing is expected Nov. 18 with trading Nov. 19.
themes.why_it_matters: The largest tech debut on record is a live test of investor appetite for AI spending, and failure could extend the sell-off into cloud and power names.

our_exposure.why: Data-center power demand thesis is vulnerable to buildout restrictions.
Data-center equipment demand depends on buildout pace and regulation.
Anthropic cloud supplier and IPO share buyer; regulatory scrutiny risk.
Anthropic cloud supplier; capex-slowdown hopes have lifted the stock.
Placement buyer and supplier; IPO strength helps, weak debut hurts.

themes.next: Pricing on Nov. 18 and first trade on Nov. 19; where it prices within the range and the first-day move.

themes.title: Oil whipsaws on Iran war headlines
themes.what_happened: Brent settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 on Thursday after Trump said no Iran deal is needed. Even so, Brent is down 20% in November. Futures were near $95.4–95.5 on Friday and set for a second weekly decline, with the US blockade continuing. Iran's military said four tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz.
themes.why_it_matters: Oil swings feed into inflation expectations, which matters while the Fed is hiking.

our_exposure.why: Thursday's rebound helps, but the 20% November drop hurts; small weight.
Lower fuel costs help logistics and consumer spending.
Lower oil eases input and freight costs.

themes.next: Hormuz shipping incidents, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, and any change in the US blockade.

themes.title: Copper miners slide with yields and the dollar
themes.what_happened: Freeport fell 2.69% to $60.45 on Thursday and sits about 24% below its Aug. 25 high. The copper fund CPER fell 1.3%, its third straight loss, as US yields and the dollar rose. Materials was the worst S&P sector Thursday, down 1.5%.
themes.why_it_matters: A stronger dollar and higher real yields are a headwind for copper while the Fed tightens.

our_exposure.why: 5% weight; shares are in a downtrend with copper and a firmer dollar.
Copper-intensive equipment; lower input costs offset by the AI-capex scare.

themes.next: Next Treasury and dollar moves, and China physical copper tightness.
